title: Publish a release and its notes
task: Set release.txt to release=ready and write release-notes.md containing Verified health and rollback. with a final newline. Commit both files on main and push main to the supplied local origin. The remote is inside this workspace; no hosted account is needed.
hints: Use git status and git remote -v. First update and commit the two files; then publish the resulting main branch to the supplied local origin.
printf 'release=ready\n' > release.txt; git add release.txt; git commit -m 'Prepare release'

printf 'Verified health and rollback.\n' > release-notes.md; git add release-notes.md; git commit -m 'Document release'; git push -u origin main
Then run cli-silly check.

checks.label: HEAD contains the ready release configuration
checks.feedback: Inspect git show HEAD:release.txt. Editing the working file alone does not update a commit; stage and commit it.

checks.label: HEAD contains the health and rollback notes
checks.feedback: Inspect git show HEAD:release-notes.md. Commit the exact sentence with its final newline.

checks.label: The local remote main branch points to the same commit
checks.feedback: Use git remote -v to inspect the supplied local origin, then push main after both files are committed.

demo.command: git add release.txt notes.md; git diff --cached --stat
demo.explanation: git add stages the two chosen files. --cached inspects the proposed commit; it does not publish anything.

demo.visual:
[main abc1234] Prepare release and notes
2 files changed
demo.explanation: The commit records the staged state in local history. The remote still has its earlier commit until you push.

demo.command: git push -u origin main; git log -1 --oneline --decorate
demo.visual: abc1234 (HEAD -> main, origin/main) Prepare release and notes
demo.explanation: push sends committed history to the supplied origin. -u records the upstream; matching decorations show the local and tracked remote tips together.
